key_insight: ML-COHP predicts DFT-derived bond strengths from frozen MACE representations, reaching 1.6–4.1% error for bonds stronger than 0.5 eV.
engineering_relevance: Rapid bond-strength estimates could accelerate analysis of grain boundaries and catalytic nanoparticles without running DFT and LOBSTER for every structure.
method: Extract frozen scalar and bond-projected vector features from a MACE foundation model.
Use a symmetric atom-pair head to correct an element-embedding pair baseline.
Combine the predictor with geometries from a fine-tuned MACE potential to examine oxygen coverage effects.
evidence_signal: Across high-entropy diborides and Pt/Pd-based systems, errors were about half those of a Gaussian-process comparator; training only on high-temperature diboride snapshots yielded 0.06 eV error on relaxed grain boundaries in about one second versus 5–51 hours for LOBSTER.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the tested chemistries and environments remains unestablished, so new applications should be checked against DFT/LOBSTER references.
paper_title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
